title: Version policy profiles and validate semantic compatibility
summary: Assemble rule families into separate evidence, lifecycle, purpose, and audience components. Domain meaning belongs in profiles, not application-name branches or one universal score.
implementation: Define profile components with immutable rule references and multiple assessments per matter.
Validate required paths, outcome implications, conflict resolvers, permissions, and budget feasibility.
Fingerprint labels, definitions, ordering, rendering, and preparation where they affect meaning.
Emit profile supersession changes without rewriting historical assessments.

acceptance.criterion: Changing meaning with unchanged output shape changes the semantic binding.
acceptance.verification: Compare same-topic and same-matter Choice profiles.

acceptance.criterion: Impossible or unauthorized profiles fail with a concrete path.
acceptance.verification: Test missing rule, undefined label, denied capability, and impossible call budget.

acceptance.criterion: Audience cadence changes leave evidence fingerprints unchanged when independent.
acceptance.verification: Compare component fingerprints and dependency sets.

tests: Two profiles can assess one matter concurrently.
A certificate for one meaning cannot qualify another.
Historical references never silently resolve to latest.
Missing conflict policy cannot fall back to last writer.
risks: Syntactically valid changes can alter behavior without triggering qualification.

reuse.application: Implement reusable families and separate audience preferences.
Bind qualification to actual question semantics and evidence preparation.
